I could not verify this by computation. I have no tool to evaluate the polynomials here, so this answer is from memory of the literature and is uncertain.

The key structural fact is that $c_j \bar{c}_j = -1$, so $\bar{c}_j = -1/c_j$. Each $a_S$ is then a signed ratio of products of the $c_j$. Repeated roots require a multiplicative coincidence among these values (for odd $k$, $a_S = \pm a_T$). Such coincidences are not generic, so the first counterexample should occur at a fairly large $k$. My recollection is that the minimal counterexample is $k = 13$, but I cannot confirm this, and a direct check of $a_S = \pm a_T$ for $k$ up to that range would be needed to settle it.

ANSWER: 13
